newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Issues at Zimbabwe OAU summit.
newsitem.headline: Issues at Zimbabwe OAU summit.

text.p: A three-day Organisation of African Unity (OAU) summit beginning in the Zimbabwean capital on Monday is expected to discuss the following issues:

-- the coup in Sierra Leone where junior army soldiers toppled the elected government of President Ahmed Tejan Kabbah. OAU foreign ministers have already condemned the coup and regional countries, led by Nigeria, are said to be preparing to reverse it.

-- the Great Lakes region where conflict simmers on even after the triumph of Laurent Kabila's Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo over long-time president Mobutu Sese Seko. Rwanda and Burundi, two states that openly backed Kabila's rebel forces, remain politically unstable under military rule.
-- Liberia's slow march to democracy. Elections in the West African country are scheduled to be held on July 19 after being postponed from May 30.

-- the slow-moving peace processes in Angola and Somalia. In the case of the former, the process has come under strain recently following UNITA complaints the government army is encroaching on its terriory. In Somalia, hope has risen after the signing of an agreement by two of the major players in the country's conflict.

-- the row between Libya and the West over the Lockerbie bombing. OAU ministers have proposed three alternatives to resolve the issue; trial of the two Libyans accused of being behind the bombing in a neutral country chosen by the U.N. Security Council, trial at the International Court of Justice in The Hague or trial at The Hague by a special criminal tribunal.
-- the restructuring of the OAU's secretariat as it seeks to transform itself into an African Economic Community by 2030.
